recipes.name: Chicken Ranch Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into 1/2 inch cubes
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in chicken and cook until no longer pink in the center, about 7 minutes. Whisk together condensed cream of chicken soup, sour cream, chiles, and ranch dressing in a bowl; spread a thin layer of the mixture into a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Spoon about 2 tablespoons of sauce into each tortilla; divide the chicken among the tortillas and sprinkle with 3/4 of the cheese. Roll the tortillas into cylinders and place seam-side-down into the baking dish. Pour the remaining sauce over the enchiladas and cover the dish with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot, about 35 minutes. Remove the foil and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. Return to the oven and cook a few more minutes until the cheese melts.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Ranch Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: Chicken ranch enchiladas combine cream of chicken soup, ranch dressing mix, and green chiles for a quick and easy dish.

video.description: These delicious baked enchiladas are filled with cheesy ranch flavor! This easy weeknight dinner can be made with leftover chicken!

review.reviewBody: I LOVED this! I am not a ranch fanatic, but I made this because my husband is. I made it exactly as the recipe is written. And it turned out fantastic! Also tastes just as good the next day for leftovers. This one is a definite keeper!

Oh my goodness! This recipe is so yum! It’s actually a recipe that is over 30 years old. It was made for me by my Mom for my first son’s baby shower! Although its been tweaked a bit. There was no ranch dressing back then, so awesome addition! Back then, we sliced our tortillas and layered them into a casserole dish like you would lasagna. We also used a rotisserie chicken and shredded the whole thing. Plus 1/2 tsp cumin mixed in with the soup mixture. 
Thought everyone might like a variation to the recipe...this way is much faster than filling/rolling tortillas! Voila! Creamy Mexican Lasagna! 
So happy you shared this classic! Excited to try it with the ranch dressing :)

This was amazing! I followed the suggestion of another reviewer and tore up the tortillas and layered the goodies. I did add granulated garlic to the chicken as it was cooking. I didn’t have the Mexican blend cheese, so I used sharp cheddar and a little bit of mozzarella and provel (St. Louisans will understand). Covered it with foil to bake. Hubby LOVED this.

Big hit! I cut the butter out n boiled the chicken and shredded. For the sauce I use 8oz of sour cream, no chilies, but I used onion n pepper blend in place. And I used homemade salsa. Served with Mexican rice and beans. Will make again same way. Thank you for sharing. A different twist to enchiladas.

What a great recipe. Everyone wanted seconds. We used "homemade" ranch dressing mix instead of the packet . We used boneless chicken thighs instead of chicken breasts(we think they are more flavorful), diced Hatch chiles, added some onions and garlic (of course).
Next we will bake this as a casserole.
Thank you for the recipe. It's a keeper

Although I usually start by making the recipe as written, this time, I made adjustments because we like things a bit spicier, and don't care for an overwhelming ranch dressing taste. 
Seasoned the chicken before cooking with salt, pepper, Mexican seasoning, and a little hot Mexican chili powder. For the sauce, added a quarter of a medium onion, chopped, and reduced the ranch dressing mix to two teaspoons. Added about a third cup of salsa. Reduced the sour cream by half and added whole milk as needed to get the desired consistency.
Thank you, Smith's Wife for sharing this recipe. We'll have this again. Easy to make and oh so tasty! This is a great recipe you can tailor to your family's tastes.

I made this using: 4 C shredded, cooked chicken breasts, 1 C Ranch Dressing from bottle (Hidden Valley is Best), 1/2 C Sour Cream, the green chilies, 1/2-2/3 C Tostito's Med. or Hot Salsa, and the cheese mixed together & divided (using 1/2 in Chicken mixture & other half to top the enchiladas before baking) .These are the BEST Enchiladas my Family & I have EVER eaten!! This Yields: between 14-17 Enchiladas depending on how much filling is used.

Made this for my husband and we both loved it. I did add a few things though to make it more filling. I mixed a can of yellow corn, a can of black beans, diced onion and a diced jalapeño with the chicken and used that for enchilada stuffing. I also swapped the green chilies for a can of mild Rotel. It wasn’t too spicy or anything and was very filling. Had some of the chicken mixture left over and we used it for tacos another night. If you want more spice, then use a can of regular Rotel instead of mild.

I have andy family loves it. Tonight I added a light coating of cumin and it turned out fantastic, nothing left. My only tip, I grill the breasts whole with the seasonings, then cube it when its done, well worth it.
I was feeling lazy and didn’t want to make a side dish to go with this. So I added cauliflower rice, sweet peppers, and black beans to make it more of a whole meal. Family Gobbled it up.
Very good flavor. I made it with only 8 oz of sour cream and added chipotle pepper seasoning. When done, topped with salsa and cilantro. Will definitely make again.
Would try shredded chicken next time.

Made as written and this was pretty good. Like others, I feel like this could use some heat so I'll add some next time. While I'm not a huge ranch fan, I really liked it in this recipe. It made it unique yet didn't overpower. Overall good recipe and one I would make again.

I made this today and it is a really good basic easy-to-make enchilada recipe. Like other reviewers, I added heat, as that's my family preference. I added onions, fajita mix and hot jalapenos when cooking the chicken. Otherwise, I made as it (I did cut down on the Ranch Mix). Our only complaint was that 35 minutes was not enough time for hot and bubbly. I added 10 minutes and it could have still gone longer in the oven but my family was waiting!! Overall we enjoyed it and I plan to make again and thinking about adding salsa to the mix. Thanks!
No changes. Yummy. Everyone wants me to make them all the time

My family liked this. You'll need about 2 lbs chicken. Added onion to chicken.. Would maybe add some jalapeños next time too, either in recipe or on top with the tomatoes and more sour cream, avacados.. etc.

Delicious. Made per the recipe after I poached the chicken breasts and shredded them. Served with chopped salad of lettuce, tomatoes and avocados tossed in blush wine vinaigrette on the side. These were yummy.

This was an absolute hit! I've been searching for months to find something my picky stepsons will eat, and this disappeared so fast I was upset I didn't double the recipe! FYI, listened to a few suggestions and only used half of the ranch as to not overpower it. A win!
This was fantastic. Added jalapenos and chopped green onions on top to spice it up. Will be putting jalapenos in each one next time. This is definitely a keeper!
Easy and tasty! A keeper.
